Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: South Africa has active cross-border remittance/payment corridors with digital providers (e.g., Mukuru and other fintech/remittance platforms) supporting cross-border digital transfers in the region ([CIGI policy brief](https://www.cigionline.org/documents/3552/Sithole_FDF_PB_final.pdf)).  Public evidence of South Africa's participation in pan-African interoperable instant payment systems (e.g., PAPSS) via official announcements was limited/early-stage in readily available sources, indicating partial/limited cross-border instant interoperability.
revision_notes: The cited CIGI brief only discusses general remittance corridors and did not itself substantiate the 'No' score. Fetched and read operator/industry sources show South Africa's BankservAfrica operates the Transactions Cleared on an Immediate Basis (TCIB) scheme, a real-time cross-border instant payment rail live since 2021 with operational corridors between South Africa and Zambia (Feb 2024), South Africa and Zimbabwe, and across the Common Monetary Area (South Africa, Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini) via FNB (Nov 2024), processing tens of thousands of transactions monthly by 2025. Separately, South Africa formally joined Afreximbank in February 2026, gaining eligibility for PAPSS, though as of the June 2026 PAPSS network coverage document South Africa remains in the 'Extended Network' for inbound-only receipt and is not yet a live direct participant; full PAPSS integration is targeted for mid-2026 but not yet confirmed complete. Recalculated to 4 (Partially functional): cross-border instant payments are operational through specific regional corridors (TCIB/SADC) rather than fully functional across all borders/PAPSS.
revised_comments: South Africa's instant payment infrastructure supports cross-border transfers through the Transactions Cleared on an Immediate Basis (TCIB) scheme operated by BankservAfrica, with live real-time corridors to Zambia, Zimbabwe and the Common Monetary Area (Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini), settling payments within 60 seconds. South Africa also formally joined Afreximbank in February 2026, giving its banks a pathway into the continent-wide Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), though direct PAPSS participation (as opposed to inbound-only receipt via the Extended Network) is still being finalised. Cross-border instant payment functionality is therefore partially functional, operating in specific regional corridors rather than across all African markets.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: POPIA requires responsible parties to notify the Information Regulator and affected data subjects "as soon as reasonably possible" after becoming aware of a security compromise involving personal information (Section 22), creating a mandatory breach notification framework ([Information Regulator](https://inforegulator.org.za/poPIA/);[DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World – South Africa](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=ZA)).
revision_notes: Original source (Information Regulator homepage) could not be re-fetched directly (timeout) but its content is corroborated by the Regulator's own fact sheet and the POPIA statutory text, both fetched and read. Section 22 of POPIA (Act 4 of 2013) obliges a responsible party to notify both the Information Regulator and affected data subjects as soon as reasonably possible after discovering a security compromise involving personal information; the Regulator's August 2025 fact sheet confirms there is no risk threshold and reporting is mandatory with no discretion. Score of 3 (Mandatory) confirmed.
revised_comments: South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA), Act 4 of 2013, imposes a mandatory data breach notification requirement under Section 22: responsible parties must notify both the Information Regulator and affected data subjects as soon as reasonably possible after discovering that personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person. The Information Regulator has confirmed there is no materiality or risk threshold, meaning all security compromises involving payment or other personal data must be reported, with notifications now submitted through the Regulator's eServices portal.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) establishes general data protection obligations applicable to payment providers processing personal information, including lawfulness, purpose limitation, and security safeguards, and has been in full effect since 1 July 2021 ([Information Regulator](https://inforegulator.org.za/poPIA/);[DLA Piper Data Protection Laws of the World – South Africa](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=ZA)).
revision_notes: DLA Piper's country page (last modified February 2026) and the POPIA statutory text confirm POPIA is a general data protection law covering all personal information processing (including by payment providers) rather than legislation with provisions specific to payment transaction data. No dedicated payment-data-specific statute was found. Score of 2 (General Data Protection Legislation) confirmed.
revised_comments: South Africa's data protection regime rests on the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA), Act 4 of 2013, a general data protection law that applies to the processing of personal information by any responsible party, including payment service providers, but contains no provisions specific to payment transaction data. POPIA sets out general conditions for lawful processing, security safeguards and data subject rights that extend to payment data as a subset of personal information, without a dedicated payment-data regime.
